servinfosub.title: General Description
servinfosub.ptxt: Soot in the GPF is burned off naturally when the GPF temperature is higher than specified temperature and fuel cut is performed at a speed higher than the specification (on condition that emission contains oxygen).

servinfosub.title: Forced Regeneration
servinfosub.ptxt: When ECM judges that the accumulation of the soot has exceeded the specification, ignition timing is retarded to raise GPF temperature so that the GPF is regenerated by burning off the accumulated soot.

Depending on the state of the soot elimination, further rise of exhaust temperature is required. When the temperature rise is necessary, ECM turns on GPF warning light in the combination meter, indicates “DRIVE TO REGENERATE GPF” on information display and requests the driver to fulfill the following driving.

item.ptxt: Vehicle speed: 50 km/h (31 mile/h) or higher

servinfosub.title: After-Sales Regeneration
servinfosub.ptxt: Regeneration of GPF by burning off the accumulated soot using SUZUKI scan tool is called “After-sales Regeneration”.
ECM informs necessity of “After-sales Regeneration” by turning on GPF warning light, indicating “DRIVE TO REGENERATE GPF” on information display. At the same time, ECM detects DTC P2463 or P24A4.

While performing “After-sales Regeneration”, GPF temperature rises by raising engine speed and retarding ignition timing. Further, lean A/F ratio is forcedly generated for burning off the accumulated soot.
In either case, “After-sales Regeneration” is necessary when ECM is replaced.
For process of “After-sales Regeneration”, refer to Gasoline Particulate Filter (GPF) After-Sales Regeneration:K14D .
